title.quote: Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting
title.justification: Title at the top of the paper
title.value: Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting

extractions.description: The paper proposes an active forgetting mechanism during pretraining of masked language models (RoBERTa-base), resetting the token embedding layer every K updates, to create PLMs that adapt quickly to new languages. Models are pretrained on English CC100, adapted to new languages with 5M tokens, task-adapted on MultiNLI/SQuAD, and evaluated zero-shot on XNLI, MLQA, XQuAD. Additional experiments cover multilingual pretraining and forgetting frequency.

type.quote: Experiments with RoBERTa show that models pretrained with our forgetting mechanism not only demonstrate faster convergence during language adaptation, but also outperform standard ones in a low-data regime
type.justification: The paper runs pretraining and adaptation experiments and reports benchmark numbers.
